rules: Prefer a shared remote endpoint over a locally spawned process.
A local server runs as one process shared across agents; multiple hosts must not each spawn their own instance of the same server.
A local server is started by the plugin or skill that needs it, not eagerly at session start, so no process is running for a session that never uses it.

A coding host named in pluginOnly gets MCP servers from plugins: its own official marketplace, then its community marketplace, then an ah-* plugin. The sync writes no direct entry there unless pluginOnly lists it with a reason.
activationPolicy.note: Recorded from an explicit owner preference on 2026-08-04: local MCP processes were multiplying across hosts and costing CPU and memory for sessions that never invoked them. activationMode carries this per server. 'shared-remote' means the fleet talks to one hosted endpoint and starts nothing locally. 'on-demand-local' means a local process is permitted, but only invoked through an owning capability, and only when that capability is used. A local server that would be eagerly started by every host at session start does not satisfy this policy regardless of how its activationMode reads.

pluginOnly.note: Owner direction 2026-11-04: no direct MCP entries beyond what a host needs, on every coding host. Each key under hosts is a plugin-only host, and its value lists the only direct entries allowed there, with the reason. pluginOwnersByHost on each server records which plugin carries it. tests/Test-PluginOnlyMcp.ps1 fails on any other entry. Hosts not listed here keep the older write-everything behaviour.

protocolRevisionNote: Every server carries a `protocol` block establishing which MCP revision it actually speaks, probed rather than assumed. This exists because `transport: "http"` stopped being informative once the 2026-07-28 revision made the core stateless: a 2025-11-25 server and a 2026-07-28 server are both 'http' and are not wire-compatible. `revision: null` is a legitimate recorded state meaning 'could not be established', and it must say why -- it is never a placeholder for an unchecked entry. mcpServers.notes: Official Devin MCP server (https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-mcp): Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.devin.ai/mcp, bearer service-user key (cog_). An org-scoped service-user key resolves its organization automatically; the helper still sends X-Org-Id org-d986482cea0c49689c6c9a590ecbdf7b so an enterprise key or PAT targets the same org. Tools cover session create/search/interact/gather, playbooks, knowledge, schedules, integrations, Devin Review and DeepWiki. Spend guard: the MCP client receives the raw key, so the ACU cap and the concurrency cap in dispatchPolicy.devin-cloud are enforced only by the dispatcher adapter, never on this lane. Sessions created through devin_session_create must pass max_acu_limit 10 and the agenthub tag by convention. Beyond that, the documented Devin-side controls are organization-level ACU limits (https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/org-acu-limits), user-level ACU limits (https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/user-acu-limits), both monthly caps, and the v3 Organization max_session_acu_limit field, a per-session limit on the organization. The owner has not yet set an org-level per-session limit. Nothing in AgentHub enforces any of these on MCP-created sessions. Deployed 2026-11-19 as a user-scope Claude entry with the headersHelper command; see protocol.verification. The service-user key expires 2027-02-17.
